segments: The Chronography of Barhebraeus.
for this reason, many were perishing.
Because when he noticed someone who recognized him,
he would send without mercy and kill him.
And he was not very concealed,
because he would go about with well-known men who were his confidants.
And on this account, whenever he passed by,
people would flee from before him.
For even a man with his wife at night was afraid to speak careless conversation;
for they feared lest he be with them in the house, or in the embrasure on the roof,
because he was seen climbing into the embrasures on the roof and on the walls of people's courtyards.
He was exceedingly concerned to hear the private matters being transacted,
not only in his own domain,
but also in those of the rest of the kings.
It is related
that Khatun, the daughter of Sultan Qilij Arslan {OCR?},
the one who was called "the woman of Khilat",
came to Baghdad on her way to make the pilgrimage at Mecca.
And he was told about her beauty,
and he sent to her the old women of his palace to betroth her.
She, however, made the excuse that she had a husband,
and that this could not be.
And she left and went to Mecca,
and she intended to return by way of Syria and go to her country out of fear of him.
And the caliph al-Nasir also reasoned that she was prepared to do so,
and he sent with her company a troop of soldiers,
as if they too were going to worship.
And when she wished to go by the other way,
they restrained her,
and brought her by force back to Baghdad.
And as soon as she arrived,
the news of her husband's death arrived.
How he died, God knows.
And he sent and brought her into the palace,
and took her as wife.
And he loved her so very much,
that when she longed to have a court and garden resembling the one she had in Khilat,
he took the designs from her,
and that very night sent and summoned the vizier,
and gave him the plan of the court and the garden.
And the latter went out at once and prepared two hundred architects and two thousand laborers,
and prepared bricks and plaster in abundance.
And they built all day, each one on one side,
and took ready-made doors from other portals of the palace,
and set them up on the new portals, which they had left according to the dimensions of the doors.
